title: Flexural Altermagnetism
authors: Songbo Li, Jinxiong Jia, Zeyu Li, Xudong Zhu, Jiaqi An, Feitong Chu, Songbo Zhang, Wenguang Zhu, Hualing Zeng, Zhenhua Qiao
abstract: We establish flexural deformation as a versatile route for engineering altermagnetism in two-dimensional collinear antiferromagnets. By tailoring the flexure, we selectively break different symmetries to realize altermagnetic states with distinct wave symmetries and reverse their spin splitting. A tight-binding model and first-principles calculations for monolayer MnPS3 demonstrate d- and i-wave states and a switchable transverse spin current in the d-wave state.
summary: This work demonstrates that mechanical bending (flexure) can be used as a powerful tool to engineer altermagnetic states in 2D antiferromagnets like MnPS3. By controlling the lattice curvature, the researchers can selectively break symmetries to achieve different spin-splitting patterns and even reverse the spin-splitting sign, enabling mechanical control over spin-current properties.
main_problem: The paper establishes flexural deformation as a versatile, mechanical route to engineer and control altermagnetism in two-dimensional collinear antiferromagnets.
main_result: By tailoring the flexure, the authors demonstrate the realization of distinct altermagnetic states (d-wave and i-wave) and show that the spin splitting can be reversibly switched by changing the symmetry-related flexural configuration.
method: The study employs a combination of theoretical modeling, using a tight-binding model built on a honeycomb supercell, and validating concepts with first-principles DFT calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is monolayer MnPS3, modeled as a 2D collinear antiferromagnet. The theoretical framework utilizes spin-layer-group symmetry analysis and incorporates mechanical strain via out-of-plane height and in-plane displacement fields.
key_observables: Momentum-dependent spin splitting ($\Delta E(\mathbf{k})$), transverse spin-splitter response ($\sigma_{z\perp}$ and $R_{xy}$), and the wave symmetry (d-wave, i-wave) of the resulting altermagnetic state.
important_parameters: The degree and type of flexural deformation, which selectively breaks specific symmetries of the lattice.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the tight-binding model approximation and the use of DFT/Hubbard-U for electronic structure calculations, along with the relaxation-time approximation for transport properties.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mechanism of flexural AM, showing lattice configurations for different states (AM-A, AM-B, i-wave) and corresponding spin-resolved band structures and momentum-resolved spin splitting patterns.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the concept of AM via symmetry breaking, then detailing the theoretical model using flexural deformation, presenting results for d-wave and i-wave states in MnPS3, and finally demonstrating the switchable transverse spin-current response.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the concept of using mechanical strain (flexure) to tune electronic and magnetic properties is highly relevant to open quantum systems and spintronics, offering a pathway for reconfigurable quantum devices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Flexural altermagnetism and spin-splitting rever- sal. (a) Spin-degenerate antiferromagnet (AFM) state. (b) and (c) Two symmetry-related flexural altermagnet (AM) configurations with reversed spin splitting. The upper and lower panels show the real-space spin configurations and spin- resolved bands, respectively. Red and blue denote opposite spins. The spin–space operation S0 transforms AM-A into AM-B, reversing the spin splitting. The table lists representa- tive spin-exchanging spatial operations of two types, Ad and Aa, distinguished by their action on the in-plane momentum.

FIG. 2. Tight-binding model realization of flexural altermagnetism and spin-splitting reversal. (a1)–(d1) Lattice configurations of the flat AFM, d-wave AM-A, d-wave AM-B, and i-wave AM, respectively. (a2)–(d2) Corresponding spin-resolved band structures. Red and blue denote spin-up and spin-down bands, respectively. (a3)–(d3) Momentum-resolved spin splitting of the 25th band, ∆E(k) = E↑(k) −E↓(k). The splitting vanishes for the flat AFM, and (a3) also indicates the Brillouin zone and high-symmetry momentum path.

FIG. 3. First-principles realization of flexural altermagnetism and spin-splitting reversal in monolayer MnPS3. (a1)–(d1) Spin-resolved band structures of the flat AFM, d-wave AM-A, d-wave AM-B, and i-wave AM, respectively. Red and blue denote spin-up and spin-down bands, respectively. (a2)–(d2) Corresponding momentum-resolved spin splitting of the fourth-highest occupied band, ∆E(k) = E↑(k) −E↓(k).

FIG. 4. Flexure-controlled spin-current response in mono- layer MnPS3. (a) Schematic of the nonrelativistic spin-splitter effect in the d-wave AM, where an in-plane electric field Ex generates opposite transverse spin-channel currents. (b) An- gular dependence of the transverse spin conductivity σz ⊥at ∆µp = −125 meV. Red and blue indicate positive and negative responses, respectively. (c) Transverse spin conductivity σz xy and (d) spin-splitter ratio Rxy as functions of the chemical- potential shift ∆µ for AM-A (red) and AM-B (blue). Negative (positive) ∆µ corresponds to p-type (n-type) doping.
